summary: This bill authorizes the Attorney General to award grants to states, territories, and localities to improve data collection and surveillance of opioid-related overdoses, including postmortem toxicology testing, data linkage, and training for law enforcement, and requires the Drug Enforcement Administration to develop uniform reporting standards for drug data and submit a specific funding request for the Fentanyl Signature Profiling Program.

scores.thoughts: This bill is primarily focused on improving data collection and law enforcement capabilities related to opioid-related overdoses and drug trafficking. It aims to enhance the tracing of drugs, processing of samples, and tracking of criminals involved in drug activity, particularly through the darknet. This directly supports stricter enforcement and better understanding of drug-related issues.

The bill provides grants to law enforcement agencies and forensic laboratories for training, upgrading systems to trace drugs, and training to trace criminals through the darknet. It also mandates training for Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers on coordinating drug-related activity. These provisions clearly aim to strengthen policing and enhance the ability to prosecute drug-related crimes, aligning with a stricter justice approach.
